fields.label: Details for MOF synthesis via microwave
fields.placeholder: Microwave synthesis involves placing all reactants in a sealed vial and exposing them to microwave irradiation, often under stirring, to achieve rapid and uniform heating, significantly accelerating the reaction rate and efficiency.

fields.label: Details for MOF synthesis via solvothermal reaction
fields.placeholder: A solvothermal reaction involves sealing all reactants in a reaction vial—often an autoclave—and heating the mixture in an oven to elevated temperatures, typically under autogenous pressure, to promote the reaction in a solvent medium.

fields.label: Details for MOF synthesis via heating/stirring
fields.placeholder: A heating reaction typically involves combining all reactants in a single vial and applying heat on a heating plate under continuous stirring to promote the reaction. When no heating is applied, the reaction proceeds at room temperature under stirring to ensure homogeneity and proper mixing of components.

fields.label: Details for MOF synthesis via mechanochemical reaction
fields.placeholder: Mechanochemical synthesis of MOFs involves inducing chemical reactions through the direct absorption of mechanical energy, typically using high-speed ball mills or reactive extruders. In this solvent-free or solvent-minimized approach, substrates are intimately mixed at the sub-micrometre scale, with constant surface renewal and localized heating accelerating the reaction. The process is highly dependent on milling parameters such as frequency, time, and vessel material, which influence both reaction kinetics and product outcome.

fields.label: Details for MOF synthesis via sonochemical reaction
fields.placeholder: Sonochemical synthesis of MOFs utilizes high-energy ultrasound irradiation to induce chemical reactions through acoustic cavitation - the rapid formation, growth, and collapse of microscopic bubbles. This process generates extreme local temperatures and pressures, creating transient hot spots that provide the energy needed to initiate or accelerate reactions. Ultrasound also enhances mixing, deagglomerates particles, and activates solid surfaces, enabling efficient MOF formation often under mild macroscopic conditions.

fields.description: If you cannot identify your procedure under the existing ones, please describe it here.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via dipping processes
fields.placeholder: A dipping reaction in a SURMOF system typically involves the automated or semi-automated sequential immersion of substrates into separate reaction solutions to enable layer-by-layer film growth. Between dipping steps, cleaning processes such as dip cleaning, ultrasonication, or spray cleaning are employed to remove unreacted species and ensure film quality. The process is usually carried out at room temperature, though heating can be applied if needed.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via spin coating
fields.placeholder: A spin-coating reaction for SURMOF or thin film formation involves the sequential application of reaction solutions—typically using a pipette—onto a substrate, which is then accelerated to a defined spinning speed to uniformly distribute the solution and remove unreacted material from the surface. This layer-by-layer process enables controlled film growth and is typically carried out at room temperature. The method can be performed either manually or in an automated setup.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via spraying processes
fields.placeholder: A spraying method for SURMOF thin film formation involves the sequential application of reaction and rinsing solutions onto a substrate, typically using airbrush pistols in manual setups. This layer-by-layer process can be carried out manually or in an automated system and is performed exclusively at room temperature.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via vapor assisted processes
fields.placeholder: Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) for SURMOF or MOF thin film formation involves the reaction of vapor-phase precursors on a substrate, resulting in film growth through surface-mediated reactions. The process is carried out at elevated temperatures using an oven.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via pump set-up
fields.placeholder: A SURMOF reaction via pump setup involves the automated or semi-automated sequential delivery of reaction and cleaning solutions into a reaction compartment containing the substrate, using a microfluidic system. The solutions are pumped in and out in a defined sequence, with controlled resting times to allow surface reactions to occur. Heating can be applied depending on the design of the reaction compartment.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via flow cell
fields.placeholder: A SURMOF reaction using a flow cell involves the sequential introduction of reaction and cleaning solutions through a microfluidic channel system, with the substrate positioned within the flow cell. The solutions are flowed over the substrate in a defined sequence with controlled resting times to enable surface reactions. Heating can be applied via a heating plate placed beneath the flow cell.

fields.placeholder: A SURMOF reaction via pump setup involves the automated or semi-automated sequential delivery of reaction and cleaning solutions into a reaction compartment containing the substrate, using a microfluidic system. The solutions are pumped in and out in a defined sequence, with controlled resting times to allow surface reactions to occur. Heating can be applied depending on the design of the reaction compartment.

fields.label: Details for SURMOF synthesis via flow cell
fields.placeholder: A SURMOF reaction using a flow cell involves the sequential introduction of reaction and cleaning solutions through a microfluidic channel system, with the substrate positioned within the flow cell. The solutions are flowed over the substrate in a defined sequence with controlled resting times to enable surface reactions. Heating can be applied via a heating plate placed beneath the flow cell.

Purpose: Reproduce the synthesis of MOCOF-1-(OH)₂·HOTf
Reference: BMI-130; 5 mL vessel instead of 8 mL; less vacuum; No CHCl3 rinse; EtOH instead of MeOH
Conclusions: Desired structure, excellent yield, purity not confirmed yet

Reaction
RT  23.4 °C, 30 % RH
5 mL Schlenk bomb, Dewar flask, liq. N₂
Add [Co(ttpp)(pba)2] (OTf)
Add DHTA
Sonicate
Add H₂O
Add PhNO₂
Add dioxane
Swirl and sonicate → dark green solution + few yellow solids
Freeze (liquid N₂, gradually, then 3 min)
Add BzOH quickly (A small amount spilled)
Pump (6.2x10-2 mbar, 1 min) [better to have less than 10-2]
Thaw (water bath, 3 min)
FPT x 2 (7.4 * 10⁻², 8.3 * 10⁻²)
Heat (preheated oven), o/w → Brown-red precipitate + Faint yellow solution
